Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: I assessed the twelve newly delivered stratum robustness comparisons. All show very large, consistent associations for the two central dataset-specific relationships. For outcome_014, feature_027=1 versus 0 is associated with a markedly higher, less negative dependency score across high and low extremes of feature_066 (H175: +0.804 [0.759, 0.848]; H176: +0.799 [0.751, 0.847]), feature_056 extremes (H179: +0.785 [0.744, 0.827]; H180: +0.835 [0.793, 0.878]), the common feature_063=level_001 stratum (H183: +0.805 [0.779, 0.832]), and the feature_019=level_002 stratum (H185: +0.796 [0.769, 0.823]). For outcome_001, feature_050=1 versus 0 is associated with a raw negative contrast, i.e. stronger dependency, across the same measured strata, as reflected by positive signed estimates under direction -1: H177 +0.784 [0.738, 0.830], H178 +0.754 [0.712, 0.797], H181 +0.793 [0.745, 0.841], H182 +0.766 [0.726, 0.806], H184 +0.783 [0.759, 0.807], and H186 +0.778 [0.753, 0.803]. These lower bounds far exceed the applicable clinical thresholds derived from a 10% magnitude of the relevant outcome scale, approximately 0.0093 for the positive outcome_014 contrasts and 0.0415 for the outcome_001 contrasts registered as direction -1. From a critical-review perspective, multiplicity from repeated subgroup checks is not a serious threat here because the effects are extremely large and directionally stable, and the central associations were already independently validated (H14 for feature_027 with outcome_014; H88 for feature_050 with outcome_001). There is no evidence of leakage or coding artifact in the reported Welch intervals; cells are adequately populated. The main limitation remains scope: these are dataset-specific associations within measured eligibility definitions, not causal claims or evidence for external generalizability. I did not request further validation because no unexpected attenuation or contradiction appeared, and additional independent validation of already enormous and consistent estimates would not materially change the conclusion.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

record.narrative:
Synthesis assessment: I reassessed H166 because it has a response deadline. H166 tested a feature_054-by-feature_050 interaction for outcome_014 among feature_027=0 samples. The signed discovery estimate was +0.0122 with 95% interval [-0.0330, +0.0574] (R130), and independent validation was smaller and much wider, +0.0071 [-0.0629, +0.0771] (R142). Both intervals include zero, and the validation lower bound is far below any clinically meaningful positive effect threshold for outcome_014 under this hypothesis direction. Thus the validation does not support the discovery signal; it is consistent with a null interaction. I reject and close H166. This strengthens the decision to close the feature_054 heterogeneity line for outcome_014, because the broader feature_054-by-feature_050 interaction claim H139 also failed independent validation, and the more controlled H166 check is null in both discovery and validation.

The supported dataset-level picture remains centered on two very large associations. First, feature_027=1 versus 0 is associated with a much higher outcome_014 CRISPR dependency score. The central validated claim is H14: discovery +0.796 [0.776, +0.816] and validation +0.802 [0.775, +0.829]. This association also persists in many measured strata with lower bounds far above the relevant clinical threshold. Second, feature_050=1 versus 0 is associated with a raw negative outcome_001 contrast, i.e. stronger dependency, represented as positive signed estimates for claims registered with direction -1. The central validated claim is H88: discovery +0.784 [0.765, +0.803] and validation +0.805 [0.774, +0.836], with many stratum-specific confirmations also having lower bounds far above threshold. These conclusions are associations within the supplied dataset and specified eligibility definitions; they do not establish causality, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.

Negative or closed findings include the feature_054 heterogeneity line: H166 and the related H139 interaction line are not supported. Other negative findings include numerous binary predictors screened against the central outcomes, where intervals either crossed zero and were too imprecise or produced effects far below clinically meaningful magnitude. H13 is an instructive negative example for outcome_013: the discovery positive estimate was not reproduced by independent validation. H117 remains underpowered and is closed as unresolved rather than strongly accepted; direction was similar across discovery and validation, but both intervals were very wide and did not clear clinical relevance.

Remaining uncertainty is mostly about scope rather than the central associations themselves: whether the large feature_027-to-outcome_014 and feature_050-to-outcome_001 associations extend to additional measured strata, whether the opaque features have interpretable biological meaning, and whether any smaller subgroup heterogeneity remains undetected. The most informative next analysis is to execute the already registered active robustness checks H187-H198, which test the two central associations across additional large strata defined by feature_024 extremes and high-prevalence nominal levels of feature_028, feature_036, feature_048, and feature_009. If those lower bounds continue to clear clinically relevant thresholds, the internal conclusion is broad robustness within measured dataset strata; if one or more strata attenuate or reverse, the conclusion should be narrowed to specific eligibility regions. I did not request additional validation because the central claims have already been independently validated, the active comparisons have not yet produced new discovery-level claims requiring validation, and the H166 validation result is confirmatory null rather than a candidate for rescue.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All twelve new stratum-specific comparisons provide valid, adequately powered Welch estimates for the two central dataset associations. For outcome_014, feature_027=1 versus 0 is associated with a very large positive signed estimate under direction +1, i.e. a much higher/less negative dependency score, in feature_024 extremes and in the feature_028=level_003, feature_036=level_002, feature_048=level_003, and feature_009=level_003 strata. All lower bounds are far above the approximately 10%-of-scale clinical threshold previously used for outcome_014 (+0.0093) and far above zero; even with multiplicity adjustment for 12 comparisons, the evidence remains decisive. Therefore H187, H189, H191, H193, H195, and H197 are accepted and closed as dataset-specific stratum robustness checks. For outcome_001, feature_050=1 versus 0 is associated with a large positive signed estimate under direction -1, meaning a raw negative contrast and therefore stronger dependency, in the analogous strata. All lower bounds are far above the approximate 10%-of-scale clinical threshold for these direction -1 outcome_001 claims (+0.0415) and far above zero. Thus H188, H190, H192, H194, H196, and H198 are accepted and closed. A critical limitation is redundancy: H191/H193 and H192/H194 have identical estimates and cell counts, consistent with feature_028=level_003 and feature_036=level_002 defining the same or nearly the same subset. This does not invalidate the accepted associations, but it means these are not independent confirmations and should not be counted as separate stratum-specific evidence. Overall, the new results extend the central validated findings—feature_027 with much higher outcome_014 and feature_050 with stronger outcome_001 dependency—across the newly tested measured strata without attenuation. They remain associations within the supplied dataset and specified eligibility definitions, not causal, mechanistic, or externally generalizable claims. No independent validation is requested: the central associations were already independently validated, the new stratum effects are enormous and highly consistent, and an additional validation would not materially alter the scientific conclusion.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
Synthesis assessment. The only response deadline is H117, which tests whether feature_006=1 versus 0 is associated with a higher signed outcome_014 score among feature_027=1 samples. The discovery estimate was modest and imprecise: +0.026 with 95% interval [-0.036, +0.088] (R144). The requested independent validation had a larger point estimate but remained extremely uncertain: +0.057 with interval [-0.050, +0.163] (R155). The comparison cells are small, especially the exposed cell (29 versus 384 in validation; 22 versus 371 in discovery), and the feature_006 exposure is rare overall. Validation did not provide a clinically meaningful lower bound for outcome_014 under this positive-direction claim. Using the approximate 10%-of-scale threshold used for outcome_014 positive effects, the validation lower bound is far below +0.0093 and also below zero. Therefore I do not upgrade H117 to accept. I also do not reject it strongly, because the confidence interval remains compatible with a clinically meaningful positive effect. The appropriate conclusion is that H117 is unresolved and closed as an inadequate-precision line: the available discovery and validation evidence are directionally similar but too sparse to support or refute a meaningful feature_006 effect within the feature_027=1 stratum.

The supported within-dataset scientific picture remains centered on two very large, independently validated associations. First, feature_027=1 versus 0 is associated with a much higher outcome_014 CRISPR dependency score under the registered positive direction: discovery +0.796 [0.776, 0.816] and validation +0.802 [0.775, 0.829] (H14). Second, feature_050=1 versus 0 is associated with a raw negative outcome_001 contrast, i.e. stronger dependency, under the registered negative direction: the signed estimates are discovery +0.784 [0.765, 0.803] and validation +0.805 [0.774, 0.836] (H88). Many subgroup strata for these two central relationships are accepted and far exceed the relevant clinical thresholds, although some are nearly duplicate stratum definitions and should not be counted as independent confirmations.

Negative or unsupported lines are now better characterized. The feature_054 heterogeneity line for outcome_014 is not supported: the broader interaction H139 failed independent validation, and the more focused H166 interaction check was null in both discovery and validation. Numerous screened binary predictors remain null or imprecise relative to their outcome scales. H13 is a clear discovery-only example for outcome_013: it did not survive independent validation. H117 is another low-prevalence, low-power line where validation neither rescues nor decisively refutes the signal.

The main remaining uncertainty is scope and modification, not the existence of the central large effects. The most informative next step is to analyze the already registered active interactions H199-H210. These test whether the feature_027-to-outcome_014 association and the feature_050-to-outcome_001 dependency association differ materially across large measured subgroup indicators: feature_028, feature_036, feature_048, feature_009, and feature_056 extremes. If those interaction estimates are null, the internal conclusion is broad within-dataset homogeneity of the two central associations across these measured strata. If a large positive signed interaction appears, the accepted conclusions should be narrowed to the relevant subgroup regions. All statements remain dataset-specific associations under specified comparisons; they do not establish causality, biological mechanism, or external generalizability. No new validation is requested, because the two central associations are already independently validated and H117 does not present a sufficiently supported candidate worth additional validation budget.

record.narrative: No claim assessments are due. The scientifically mature part of the investigation remains the two very large within-dataset associations: H14, feature_027=1 versus 0 associated with much higher outcome_014 under direction +1, and H88, feature_050=1 versus 0 associated with a raw negative outcome_001 contrast, i.e. stronger dependency, under direction -1. These have been validated and accepted, while many screened predictors are null or imprecise. The main remaining internal uncertainty is scope and effect modification, not the existence of these central associations. I therefore registered a focused follow-up interaction battery plus some high-prevalence direct associations. The interaction proposals ask whether the central feature_027-to-outcome_014 association or the feature_050-to-outcome_001 dependency association is materially different in a named subgroup than in its complement. For outcome_014 under direction +1, a positive signed interaction means the feature_027 contrast is stronger/higher in the subgroup. For outcome_001 under direction -1, a positive signed interaction means the feature_050 raw contrast is more negative in the subgroup, i.e. stronger dependency in that subgroup. These interactions cover common binary markers feature_034, feature_002, and feature_060; large common categorical strata feature_063=level_001 and feature_019=level_002; and feature_024 quartile extremes. They extend the active H199-H210 interaction battery across feature_028, feature_036, feature_048, feature_009, and feature_056 extremes. I also registered direct mean-difference hypotheses for high-prevalence binary variables feature_008 and feature_030 and for common categorical contrasts feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 and feature_048 level_001 versus level_003. These direct claims test whether measured covariates or nominal strata share large within-dataset associations with the two central outcomes rather than merely being strata for the central associations. Anticipated directions are set to 0 for the new effect-modification and direct associations because prior stratum-specific main effects were robust but interaction evidence was weak, and prior direct associations for most screened predictors were near null. Clinical interpretation will use the approximate 10%-of-outcome-scale thresholds used earlier: for positive outcome_014 contrasts and interactions, about +0.0093; for direction -1 outcome_001 stronger-dependency contrasts and interactions, about +0.0415. If an interaction lower bound exceeds its threshold, the central association is subgroup-concentrated in that measured stratum. If intervals include small values and are far below threshold, the evidence supports broad within-dataset homogeneity. If direct associations are null, they help characterize measured covariates that do not explain the central outcome differences. All statements remain dataset-specific associations, not causal, mechanistic, or externally generalizable claims. No validation is requested at this explore stage; validation should be reserved for a new candidate that independently reaches clinical-scale support.

prompt:
Iteration 15/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The twelve newly delivered discovery analyses are valid Welch comparisons with adequate cell counts and no apparent coding or eligibility errors. They serve two purposes: test whether the accepted very large outcome_014/feature_027 and outcome_001/feature_050 associations are modified by common strata, and screen a few high-prevalence predictors for new overall associations. I used the same practical 10%-of-outcome-scale thresholds used in earlier appraisals: approximately +0.0093 for positive outcome_014 contrasts/interactions and approximately +0.0415 for signed positive outcome_001 direction -1 contrasts/interactions. For interactions, a positive signed estimate means the central contrast is larger in the named subgroup than in its complement, under the registered direction. None of the interaction lower bounds reaches its relevant clinical threshold. H199, H201, H202, and H203 are near-null with intervals including zero and, in most cases, reversed point estimates; they do not support clinically meaningful positive effect modification, but the intervals remain too wide to reject every possible clinically meaningful positive interaction. I therefore record H199, H201, H202, and H203 as unresolved but closed as low-priority interaction checks. H205 and H206 are stronger evidence against the registered positive interaction direction: their point estimates are negative and their upper bounds are below the +0.0415 clinical threshold for outcome_001 effect modification, so clinically meaningful positive modification by feature_048=level_003 or feature_009=level_003 is not supported; reject and close. The direct battery is also mostly unsupported. H223 and H225 test feature_008=1 and feature_030=1 versus 0 for outcome_014 under positive direction. Both have small negative point estimates; although the upper bounds are compatible with clinically meaningful positive values, the evidence does not support a new broad positive association, so these remain unresolved but closed. H224 and H226 test the same exposures on outcome_001 under direction -1. H224 is near null with a reversed point estimate and an upper bound only marginally above the clinical threshold; H226 has a positive point estimate far too small and a wide interval crossing zero. Neither supports a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association; both remain unresolved but closed. H228, testing feature_063=level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_001 under direction -1, has a negative point estimate and an upper bound of +0.026, below the +0.0415 threshold, so there is no clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect; reject and close. The one new candidate is H227: outcome_014 feature_063=level_002 versus level_001, signed estimate +0.0361 with 95% Welch interval [+0.0022, +0.0701]. The point estimate is clinically plausible because it exceeds the approximate +0.0093 threshold, and the lower bound is positive, but it is below the clinical threshold and this was one of many pre-registered comparisons, so nominal significance is not enough. I request independent validation for H227 rather than accept it now. If validation produces a lower bound above the clinical threshold, H227 could be accepted as an additional dataset-specific outcome_014 association; if not, it should be closed as unsupported or imprecise. These remain within-dataset associations only, not causal or generalizable claims.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

"narrative": "Synthesis/current scientific report.

1) New validation deadline: H227.
H227 tested whether feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 is associated with a higher outcome_014 CRISPR dependency score. The discovery Welch estimate was +0.036 with a 95% interval from +0.002 to +0.070 (R190). Using the same practical 10%-of-scale threshold applied to positive outcome_014 contrasts, approximately +0.0093, the discovery point estimate is clinically plausible but its lower bound is below the clinical threshold. Independent validation gave a smaller but directionally similar point estimate, +0.027, with a validation interval from -0.022 to +0.076 (R192). The validation lower bound is not only below the clinical threshold but also below zero, so the independent evidence does not establish a clinically meaningful positive association. I therefore do not accept H227 as a new supported outcome_014 predictor. I also do not reject it, because the validation interval remains compatible with a clinically meaningful positive effect. The appropriate conclusion is that H227 is unresolved but closed as an imprecise, not-confirmed candidate: there is a hint of a positive level_002 effect in the supplied dataset, but the uncertainty is too large to conclude that the difference reaches scientific or clinical significance.

2) Supported findings in this dataset.
The strongest and independently validated within-dataset associations remain the two central relationships. First, H14 is supported: feature_027=1 versus 0 is associated with a much higher outcome_014 score, with signed estimates around +0.80 and narrow intervals in both discovery and validation. Second, H88 is supported: under the registered negative direction, feature_050=1 versus 0 is associated with a raw negative outcome_001 contrast, which means stronger CRISPR dependency on outcome_001, again with signed estimates around +0.80 and tight intervals. Many additional accepted subgroup claims show that these very large associations persist across many measured strata, but several of those strata are highly prevalent or nearly duplicate categories and should be interpreted as robustness checks rather than independent confirmations. The central conclusion is that the supplied dataset contains two unusually large, robust feature-to-outcome associations rather than a broad set of predictor effects with comparable magnitude.

3) Negative and unsupported lines.
Recent discovery results reduce the plausibility of a broad set of additional clinically meaningful predictor effects. The feature_054 heterogeneity line for outcome_014 is not supported: the broader interaction H139 failed independent validation, and the more focused H166 interaction check was null. Many tested interactions involving the two central associations showed no clinically meaningful positive effect modification. H205 and H206 are informative negative findings because their upper bounds fall below the relevant clinical threshold for outcome_001 effect modification, so positive interaction by feature_048=level_003 or feature_009=level_003 is not supported. H199, H201, H202, and H203 are near-null or imprecise and closed because they do not support clinically meaningful positive modification. The direct screen of feature_008 and feature_030 is also unsupported or imprecise for both central outcomes. H228 rejects a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association for feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_001 under the registered direction. H13 and H117 illustrate that discovery-only small signals did not survive or were not resolved by validation, especially for sparse strata or less precise comparisons.

4) Unresolved uncertainty.
The main unresolved line is not whether the two central associations exist; they are well supported within this dataset. The remaining uncertainty is their exact scope across all measured predictors and strata. H227 remains the best example of a modest residual candidate: outcome_014 may be somewhat higher for feature_063 level_002 relative to level_001, but the validation interval is too wide to support a clinically meaningful claim. Several interaction hypotheses are still unresolved and pending analysis, especially among the active pre-registered interaction battery. Some of these may be redundant because feature_028 and feature_036 appeared to define nearly identical strata in prior direct estimates, so interpretation should avoid treating duplicate strata as independent evidence. Biological meaning remains uncertain because predictor names and categorical levels are opaque labels. All statements are associations in the supplied dataset under specified comparisons, not causal effects, mechanistic claims, or claims of external generalizability.

5) Most informative next analysis.
The next analysis should concentrate on the already registered active interaction battery rather than opening new validation targets. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered discovery results are valid Welch comparisons with adequate cell counts and no apparent coding or eligibility errors. I audited them using the practical clinical-scale thresholds used in this run: approximately +0.0093 for positive outcome_014 contrasts or positive interactions under direction +1, and approximately +0.0415 for signed positive outcome_001 contrasts or positive interactions under direction -1, where signed positive outcome_001 means stronger dependency. The batch was primarily a scope test of the two accepted central associations, H14 and H88, plus a small direct screen of feature_047 and feature_055. Most results do not support clinically meaningful positive effect modification or new predictor associations. H232 rejects clinically meaningful positive outcome_001 interaction by feature_047=1 because its upper bound, +0.0386, is below the +0.0415 threshold. H234 rejects the registered positive outcome_001 interaction by feature_055=level_003; its signed interval is entirely negative, arguing against stronger dependency in that subgroup, although the reverse attenuation magnitude is not confirmed beyond clinical precision. H235 rejects a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association for feature_047 within feature_050=0 because its upper bound is +0.0338, below threshold. H239 similarly rejects a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency association for feature_055 level_003 versus level_001 within feature_050=0 because its upper bound is +0.0267, below threshold. H231, H233, H236, and H238 remain unresolved but are closed as low priority: they do not support clinically meaningful positive effects, but their intervals are wide enough or, in H236/H238, only weakly bounded near threshold so a full rejection would be overly strong. H209, H220, and H221 are also unresolved and closed because their point estimates are subthreshold or imprecise and intervals do not establish clinically meaningful positive interaction. The lower bound is positive, but it is below the clinical threshold, so the evidence supports a nominal positive interaction but not a scientifically meaningful one. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
